spike: pure-weights MX constant-multiplier feasibility (plan doc: docs/pure_weights_plan_05092026_0054.md, Phase 0)

oracle.arithmetic: qwen_ref.fp.f32_mul (qwen-ref-v2 profile) on the exact FP32 operands
oracle.note: MX decode (E2M1/E4M3 code -> exact FP32 value, E8M0 block scale as a power of two) is exact by construction; the elementwise product of an MX weight and a normal BF16 activation is exact in FP32 (weight significand <= 8 bits x activation significand 8 bits <= 16 significant bits < 24), so no rounding step exists in the datapath.

mx_sweep.coverage: E2M1 all 8 codes x 3 scales (120/127/134) x activation set; E4M3 representative codes (normals, subnormal, max, signed, -0) x activation set; activations include normal range (ef 1..254 sampled), subnormal activations (ef=0, m!=0), zero, inf, NaN

bf16_core_sweep.coverage: 3 BF16 weights (1.0, 0x4248, 0x42F6) x activation set incl. subnormal activations

aig_measurement.flow: yosys 0.67 proc/opt/techmap/opt -> abc -g AND -> opt; stat
aig_measurement.unit: AIG AND nodes (whole unit incl. special branches and output assembly)
aig_measurement.caveat: Whole-unit counts include ~100 AND of 32-bit output-select muxes that amortize per accumulator in a real dot product, and the activation-subnormal normalize (~50 AND) that amortizes per activation row. Marginal per-weight cost is lower.
structural_findings: The subnormal-result branch costs ~288 AND and is compile-time prunable per (weight, scale) pair when the generator proves the result exponent range never reaches e_res < 1 (E2M1 w=1.0 folds 334->46-class; the branch is the dominant cost).

A one-hot mux normalize beats the behavioral variable shift for weights whose product msb is not constant (E2M1 w=1.5: 419 behavioral -> 262 structural with the provably-unreachable subnormal branch deleted; pw_e2m1_ns shape).
Weights that are pure powers of two (E2M1 1.0/2.0/4.0 with reachable-normal results) collapse to 46-284 AND; the exponent path is a constant increment, the significand a wire.
The zero-weight stub is 8 AND (sign handling for the RNE -0/+0 rule), not zero silicon, in the serial-accumulation contract.
aig_measurement.generator_shape_conclusion: The generator must emit per-weight: (a) structural shifted-add product from the constant significand, (b) one-hot msb mux normalize (not variable shift), (c) constant-folded exponent increment, (d) compile-time pruned subnormal-result branch per (weight, scale) reachability, (e) shared (amortized) output-select and activation-decode per dot-product column.

chip_count_implication.basis: Measured whole-unit AND counts; marginal per-weight cost excludes amortized output-select and activation decode. Tr conversion [E]: 1 AIG AND ~ 4 transistors (NAND2, N4-class).

tr_per_param_estimated.mxfp4_typical: 650-1700 [E, from 248-419 AND whole-unit; 262 structural for w=1.5; w=1.0 pure-shift 46]

chip_count_implication.revision_note: The spike revised the earlier [E] estimate (MXFP4 ~100-150 Tr/param) UPWARD ~2-4x: the special-branch and normalize machinery, not the mantissa adder, dominates the per-weight cost at whole-unit granularity. The generator specializations (branch pruning, one-hot normalize, amortization) recover part of it; the honest 30B-A3B MXFP4 footprint is ~1.5-2.5 wafers (revised from ~1), 1T-class ~45-70 wafers (revised from ~15-22).
chip_count_implication.next_measurement: Phase 1 generator emits the amortized dot-product shape (N weights sharing one output stage and one activation decode); re-measure per-matrix AND counts on q_proj L0 to replace the whole-unit numbers with marginal ones.

provenance.labels: bit-exactness measured; AIG counts measured (generic flow, not a foundry result); Tr/param and chip counts estimated [E] from measured AND counts

audit_outcome.claim: External audit (2026-05-09): the first generator emitted a w_bits reg array indexed by runtime ports (row_i/col_i) plus a generic 8-bit shift-add multiplier on the runtime-read value -- a ROM + generic multiplier, not pure weights.
audit_outcome.fix: tools/gen_pure_weights.py now emits one pw_bf16_core #(.W_BF16(<const>)) instance per weight (weight bound at elaboration time, per-bit shift-add ifs see compile-time constants) selected by case over row_i/col_i. No w_bits array, no runtime weight read, no generic multiplier.

measurements.result: still running at >2000 s (killed; no completion in sight)

monolithic_elaboration.scaling: super-linear (roughly quadratic) in distinct parameterized specializations; hierarchy changes the cliff's shape, not its existence -- Verilator's cost is dominated by total distinct specializations per invocation
monolithic_elaboration.note: The original gate (21.2 s, 29.3 MB) measured the w_bits ARRAY form -- a cheap elaboration that did not exercise the per-weight-instance architecture at all.

row0_functional.vectors_desc: 64 pseudo-random (col, activation) probes + 8 corners (zero, min/max subnormal, min normal, 1.0, max normal, -1.0, inf) on real q_proj_l0 row 0, full FP32 product bits vs qwen_ref.fp.f32_mul

split_build_path.extrapolation_full_model: 411M weights / 1024 per row = ~401k row-module builds x ~2.6 s ~ 12 days single-threaded; embarrassingly parallel (14 cores ~ <1 day) and cacheable per matrix. Per-row SV ~0.1 MB; full 0.6B ~ 58 GB of row modules on disk.

phase1_feasibility_gate.verdict: FEASIBLE ONLY VIA SPLIT BUILDS: monolithic 2.1M-instance elaboration OOMs on a 24 GB machine (measured, both flat and hierarchical emission); per-row-module builds are linear at ~2.6 s/1024 instances and functionally exact on real ROM data. Full-model gate requires the split flow; per-matrix monolithic builds are viable only below ~32k instances.

phase1_pw_gemm_kat.contract: serial FP32 accumulation of exact constant products, BF16 RNE commit (qwen-ref-v2)
phase1_pw_gemm_kat.note: Engine handshake bug found and fixed during KAT: act_ready gated off the last k, deadlocking the row. act_ready = running; commit on the final activation.
phase1_pw_gemm_kat.architecture: pw_katslice_weights regenerated as 128 pw_bf16_core #(.W_BF16(...)) instances (row modules + case mux); no w_bits array

subnormal_result_fix.found_by: pw-split-check corner vectors on real q_proj_l0 row 0 (a=0x0001 col=792, a=0x0080 col=172)
subnormal_result_fix.bug: Subnormal FP32 RESULTS with negative significand shift (e_res_32 - msb + 22 < 0) were flushed to zero instead of RNE-rounded. The 2026-05-09 spike fix covered only the left-shift case; the spike sweep's scale range never produced a right-shift subnormal result, so 10,065 vectors missed it. Real weights do hit it.
subnormal_result_fix.fix: Mirror qwen_f32_mul's subnormal path: guard = last bit shifted out, sticky = bits below it, round up on guard && (sticky || lsb); carry-to-min-normal unreachable (p < 2^17); shifts >= 18 (bf16) / 16 (MX) round to zero. Applied to pw_bf16_core.sv, pw_const_mul_core.sv, pw_mx_dyn.sv; all lint-clean.

cycle_analysis.question: How many cycles per forward pass, and can we reduce them?

measured_baseline.pw_engine_today: qwen3_pw_gemm computes ALL per-weight products combinationally every cycle and uses one -- 1 MAC/cycle => 608,945,152 cycles/token for GEMM work alone (~10.7x the fused engine's 57.0M). The multiply is already free (wires); the serial FP32 add chain is the bottleneck.

option_1_serial_lane_chain_16x.what: Copy qwen_bf16_mac_array's bit-exactness trick: instantiate 16 constant cores per cycle, chain their exact products through the SAME serial FP32 adder in oracle k-order inside one combinational block (16 adds/cycle, identical rounding sequence).
option_1_serial_lane_chain_16x.cycles: GEMM work drops 10.7x: 608,945,152 -> 38,059,072 cycles/token; whole-token schedule ~= fused mask-ROM's measured 57,024,559 cycles/token (13t: 745,190,883).
option_1_serial_lane_chain_16x.area_cost: 16 cores per lane slot instead of 1: GEMM logic x16 (the dominant area term already; see chip_count_implication).
option_1_serial_lane_chain_16x.verdict: RECOMMENDED Phase 1 change: same arithmetic profile qwen-ref-v2, no new oracle, measured 10.7x cycle reduction on the GEMM path.

option_2_carry_save_exact_sum_tree.what: CSA tree over k products, one final FP32-normalize; changes the rounding order.
option_2_carry_save_exact_sum_tree.cost: Requires a new oracle profile (qwen-ref-v3-csa) and re-verification of all gates; saves only the add-chain latency, which option 1 already parallelizes 16x.
option_2_carry_save_exact_sum_tree.verdict: Deferred -- option 1 reaches fused-engine cycles without leaving the verified profile.

option_3_full_unroll_per_layer.what: Every weight's product network hardwired (the full pure-weights endgame): a 1024-deep dot becomes an adder tree, ~log2(1024)=10 add levels ~ single-digit cycles per dot; q_proj_l0 alone collapses from 2,097,152 serial cycles to ~12 pipeline-latency cycles.
option_3_full_unroll_per_layer.cost: Same rounding-order problem as option 2 plus the elaboration wall measured above (monolithic 2.1M-instance builds OOM; full 0.6B is ~411M instances).
option_3_full_unroll_per_layer.verdict: The 30B-A3B endgame shape, gated on a new oracle profile and the split-build flow; not a Phase 1 lever.

cycle_analysis.bottom_line: Adopt option 1: ~10.7x fewer cycles (608.9M -> 38.1M GEMM cycles/token), bit-exact under the existing qwen-ref-v2 profile, matching the fused engine's measured 57.0M cycles/token.
cycle_analysis.non_gemm_stages_note: Non-GEMM stages (softmax, norms, rope) are shared with the fused engine and already inside the 57.0M measured budget; pw changes do not touch them.

wafer_yield_redundancy.question: Wafer-scale integration will have defects; what redundancy keeps yield viable?
wafer_yield_redundancy.why_pure_weights_is_special: Weights ARE the silicon structure. A defect in a weight's constant network is a wrong multiplier bit -- the die computes a wrong model, not a dead one. There is no field repair and no re-download; redundancy must be built in and tested at manufacturing.

cited_defect_density.intel_18a: D0 < 0.40 defects/cm2 at launch (>67% die yield); volume production D0 ~ 0.1 (>90% yield) -- Vikram Sekar, 'How Foundries Calculate Die Yield' (2024-09-15), quoting Intel's Ben Sell.
cited_defect_density.repo_node: N4 (lab/scale_1t.py: 240 MTr/mm2, 0.021 um2 SRAM bitcell); D0 assumed in the 0.1-0.4 band [C] until a foundry quote exists.

layer_1_die_level_sparing.mechanism: Chip-to-chip pipeline (plan Phase 3: ~1 die per layer, activations only across boundaries). Manufacture spare dies per wafer; wafer test (JTAG scan + KAT per die: each pure-weights die runs its own layer's vectors) classifies known-good die (KGD); a defect maps the layer to a spare die via the D2D fabric's route table.
layer_1_die_level_sparing.cost: Spare-die count, not per-die area. Poisson die yield Y=e^(-D0*A) is brutal at these areas: D0=0.1/cm2 gives Y=0.0123 at a 44 mm2 reticle die and Y=8.76e-27 at 600 mm2; D0=0.4 gives Y=2.27e-08 and 5.88e-105. Conclusion: KGD selection at reticle-die granularity is necessary but nowhere near sufficient -- the primary redundancy must be INTRA-die (layers 2 and 4), with wafer-scale fabric remap routing around dead regions (Cerebras-style), because monolithic large dies are hopeless at D0 >= 0.1.
layer_1_die_level_sparing.note: The 600 mm2 die_capacity figure in evidence/multi_die_scaling.json is an upper bound; Phase 3's ~44 reticle dies for 30B-A3B MXFP4 are the real granularity.

layer_2_intra_die_expert_sparing.mechanism: MoE gives free structural redundancy: 128 experts, 8 active. Fuse spare expert regions per die; the router's remap table (burned at test, one-time) routes around a defective expert region. A defective expert = a disabled expert with its capacity re-split across survivors.
layer_2_intra_die_expert_sparing.cost: Spares consume area exactly like active experts (same constant-network economics); 10-15% spare expert capacity covers the D0 band at expert granularity because expert regions are large (~0.3-0.5 mm2 at MXFP4) and defects are point events.
layer_2_intra_die_expert_sparing.accuracy: Router remap changes the model (expert capacity split), so it must be applied in QAT or accepted as a measured accuracy delta -- flagged as a model-level decision.

layer_3_kv_and_fabric_ecc.mechanism: KV SRAM (per-layer banks, kv_placement() tiering in lab/scale_1t.py) gets SECDED ECC -- KV is runtime-written, so a failed bit cell is repaired by ECC + row remap at test. On-wafer fabric links get CRC + packet retry (activations only; weights never cross dies).
layer_3_kv_and_fabric_ecc.cost: SECDED on int8 KV ~ 1/8 check bits ~ +12.5% KV SRAM; retry buffers ~ negligible area.

layer_4_weight_network_self_test.mechanism: Every pure-weights die self-tests at boot AND at manufacturing: the die's own constant networks compute their KAT vectors (the same pw-split-check vectors, stored in a tiny per-die test ROM). A mismatching weight network is recorded in a per-die defect map; GEMM scheduling skips that output row if a spare row exists, or the die is rejected.
layer_4_weight_network_self_test.cost: Test ROM ~ KBs per die; zero runtime cost (test at boot only).
layer_4_weight_network_self_test.note: This is the pure-weights analog of DRAM post-package repair: the defect map is the spare structure.

yield_math_anchor.model: Poisson: Y = e^(-D0*A) per die; wafer usable 60,000 mm2 (lab/scale_1t.py preset 70,686 * 0.85).
yield_math_anchor.reading: At cited D0 values, per-die yield collapses exponentially with area: a 44 mm2 reticle die yields 1.2% (D0=0.1) to 2e-8 (D0=0.4). Wafer-scale viability therefore rests on fine-grained sparing + fabric remap (treat the wafer as one die with millions of small redundant units), not on KGD dies.
yield_math_anchor.labels: [C] D0 values cited (Intel 18A <0.4, volume ~0.1), [E] Poisson model standard, areas from repo constants.

wafer_yield_redundancy.bottom_line: Redundancy hierarchy, in order of importance at cited D0: (1) fine-grained intra-die sparing -- spare output rows/expert regions with per-die defect maps from boot-time weight-network self-test; (2) wafer-scale fabric remap routing around dead regions (activations only; weights never cross dies); (3) KGD reticle-die selection as the coarse fallback; (4) SECDED ECC on KV SRAM (runtime-written, repairable) + CRC/retry on fabric links. Pure-weights dies are not repairable after manufacture, so all mechanisms burn in at test; the wafer budget (1.5-2.5 wafers for 30B-A3B MXFP4) must include the spare fraction.

phase1_pw_gemm16.approved: User approved the 16-lane serial-chain engine (2026-05-09), built as NEW RTL; the 1-element engine (qwen3_pw_gemm.sv), its generator (tools/gen_pure_weights.py), and qwen_bf16_mac_array.sv are untouched.

architecture.mode_a: One pw_bf16_core per (row, col) weight grouped into 16-element k-windows; per cycle the engine supplies one 256-bit activation beat + window index and receives 16 exact FP32 products; they are chained through 16 serial qwen_f32_add calls in ascending k order inside one combinational block (the qwen_bf16_mac_array bit-exactness trick). Rounding sequence identical to the 1-element engine; IN_FEATURES/16 cycles per row => 16 MACs/cycle.
architecture.packages: Fixed module names pw_gemm16_weights_w16 (window form) / pw_gemm16_weights_b16 (batch form, emitted but engine integration deferred) so the engine RTL is matrix-agnostic; one matrix per build (split-build flow).
architecture.cycle_math: GEMM work 608,945,152 MACs/token / 16 = 38,059,072 cycles/token (vs 608.9M for the 1-element engine; fused mask-ROM reference 57,024,559 cycles/token whole-token).

pw_kat16.note: 8x16 katslice, 4 oracle sets per row; same legacy vector format as tb_pw_kat so the identical stimuli run through both engines for parity

pw_row16.note: 4 REAL q_proj_l0 rows x 1024 elements (64 windows per row, 4096 cores) vs qwen_ref.fp serial oracle; exercises window streaming, chain order across window boundaries, and BF16 RNE commit

root_cause_history.earlier_full_depth_failure_was_void: The recorded 'PW_BATCH16Q total=16 mism=256' run and the constant-1.0 probe (commit 0000) both executed against the PRE-wire-fix package (block modules missing p{c}_{s} declarations -> 1-bit IMPLICIT product wires -> zero products). obj_b16q (20:41) never produced a binary: that build died compiling the fixed package. The engine was never functionally wrong at depth.
root_cause_history.emitter_single_block_mux_bug: The 2026-09-06 block-split emitter emitted the row module's block mux unconditionally as case (col_i[cb-1:cb-bb]). For the katslice shape (16 cols -> nb=1 block, bb forced to 1) this emitted case (col_i[3:3]): cols 0..7 selected the block, cols 8..15 fell to the 512'b0 default. Measured: katslice smoke 1831/2048 mismatches with large-normal got values (partial sums of the first 8 terms). Fix: nb==1 emits assign product_o = blk0; (tools/gen_pure_weights16.py). Smoke re-passed 128/128 after the fix; the 1024-col package (nb=16, case on col_i[9:6]) is byte-identical before and after the fix (diff-verified).

codegen_wall.problem: The fixed 32,768-core package inlines into ONE ___nba_comb eval function of 308,642,897 B (__024root__297.cpp) + 308,642,555 B (__024root__295.cpp); clang++ at -Os dies on it (0-byte .o.tmp, process killed).

measured_dead_ends.output_split_cfuncs_30000: splits ___nba_sequent into ~300 chunks but NOT ___nba_comb regions -> giants remain
measured_dead_ends.inline_mult_0: Verilator dies silently (OOM) ~9 min into cvt: 32,768 unique-parameter pw_bf16_core types all stay un-inlined
measured_dead_ends.inline_mult_1: same death (instance counting is per parameterized type: every core is a 1-instance type)

codegen_wall.working_recipe: --output-split 30000 --output-split-cfuncs 30000 -CFLAGS -O0: at -O0 both 308 MB units compile to 64,047,392 / 64,047,632 B objects

phase1_pw_batch16.batch_conclusion: Batch is a KV-capacity knob, not a compute knob: mode B shares the same hardware as mode A (16k x 1seq vs 1k x 16seq), per-sequence accumulation stays strictly serial in k, and the throughput ceiling is the 16-lane 38,059,072 GEMM cycles/token. See plan doc 2026-05-09 batching addendum for the serving sweet spot (batch 8-16 short context, tiered down at 128k; int4 KV buys batch back).
